description: An immutable row-major rectangular sequence of planar positions with explicit point counts and spacing.

behavior.construction: Validate shape/type/domain in field order origin, spacing, columns, rows (vector x before y), then exact count product, then nonempty last coordinate x before y. Copy values, canonicalize all zero origins/counts to +0. Return immutable sequence; size computed, never serialized. No output-sized allocation.
behavior.sequence: size=columns*rows. i in [0,size): column=i modulo columns; row=(i-column)/columns, exact integer arithmetic. x changes fastest.
behavior.point: For each axis separately, product=roundBinary64(axisIndex*spacing); coordinate=roundBinary64(origin+product). No FMA or repeated addition. Normalize coordinate zero to +0.
behavior.empty: Either count zero gives size zero and no valid index. Validate input spacing regardless. Do not evaluate endpoint arithmetic for empty results.
behavior.coordinate_validation: For nonempty grids evaluate the last x and last y with the specified separate operations. A nonfinite product or sum rejects construction before output. Finite rounding may collapse adjacent positions at large magnitudes.
behavior.ownership: Immutable sequence detached from input arrays. Semantic pointAt(index) returns a fresh two-number binary64 value. Optional native pointInto(index,out,offset) writes exactly two coordinates after all validation. Invalid access leaves storage unchanged. Internal fields never alias writable output storage.
behavior.native_storage: Native-only optional optimization: pointInto accepts writable binary64-capable storage, with integral nonnegative offset and room for two values. Index type/domain then bounds then storage/offset validation. float32/PVector buffers are forbidden for this exact route. This is transport, not a second operation or serialized shape.
behavior.units: Caller-defined planar coordinate units shared by origin/spacing/output. No canvas, axis handedness or drawing transform is implicit; increasing column increases x and increasing row increases y.
behavior.numerics: IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even on basic add/multiply, separate rounding. Counts <= signed 32-bit max; size/index <= 2^53-1. Native numeric booleans are not numbers. NaN/infinity rejected.
behavior.complexity: Construction and indexed access O(1) work/storage; complete traversal O(size). Materialization is optional caller work with explicit resource ownership.
behavior.serialization: Serialize only origin, spacing, columns, rows, matching input_schema; each serialization is detached. Reconstruct through the same validated constructor. Reject an extra size field rather than trust or retain redundant derived state.
behavior.source_conversion: Example-only: source cell counts must be positive, point count=cell count+1 must fit the axis bound, spacing=binary64(span/cell count). No hidden endpoint-inclusion or span conversion policy.
behavior.numeric_validation: For JSON-like inputs, reject unknown/missing keys and vector shapes before numeric validation. Check both origin components, both spacing components, columns, rows, in order. JSON Schema integer permits integral number values; booleans are never numeric. All components and native indices must be finite. Different failures within this phase all use INVALID_INPUT.
behavior.integer_validation: Compute count product without overflow; accept only exact products <= 2^53-1. Use mathematical modulo and quotient for index decomposition before exact index-to-binary64 conversion. Never narrow flat indices to 32 bits.
behavior.native_representations: Java accepts Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double numeric values; BigDecimal/BigInteger/custom Number values require explicit caller conversion and are rejected. JavaScript accepts JSON-like passive records/arrays and binary64 output arrays; output slot previous contents are irrelevant, ordinary extensible holes are accepted. Active accessors/proxies are not interchange data and their side effects are outside the contract. Python uses int/float inputs (never bool), and exact builtin list or array(d) output storage.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong shape, unknown/missing keys, invalid numeric type/domain, nonfinite component, count outside representable domain.
errors.COORDINATE_OVERFLOW: Nonempty last-coordinate multiply or add is nonfinite.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index not a finite safe nonnegative integer (booleans excluded).
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid index representation but index >= size.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: Optional native pointInto storage/offset is not writable binary64-capable space for two coordinates.

origin.evidence: Caller placement input; negative origins needed for overscan in pelines.

spacing.evidence: Positive pitch separates position placement from mark length. No common visual range from the current variants.

columns.evidence: circlesAlpha uses source cell counts requiring +1 conversion; paraisooscuro uses point counts. 32-bit domain is a representation design choice.

rows.evidence: Same count convention as columns; independent axis counts.

design_divergences: Point counts instead of source-dependent cell counts.
Compact immutable descriptor instead of host PVector arrays or immediate point drawing.
Specified row-major indexed binary64 computation rather than unspecified/repeated-addition source float loops.
Invalid/empty/overflow and representation bounds are explicit library design choices, not measured artistic ranges.

reproduction.acceptance: circlesAlpha: verify cell-to-point count and canvas-span extrema after explicit conversion. paraisooscuro: verify 60x60 count only; exact origin/pitch/endpoints are not established by its note. Row-major order is the library contract, not a source fact. No whole-sketch raster reproduction is claimed; CP1 native rendering is recorded separately in cp1_example.

cp1_example.scope: Actual JAVA2D example/edit/transfer only; motivating corpus baseline suites and other hosts are not certified.

review.result: Accepted operation boundary; six clarifications resolved in this contract.
